question: to the Commission Catarina Martins (The Left) Subject:

Storm Kristin caused damage to essential infrastructure in a number of areas of Portugal. One hundred days later, many households are still missing roofs, have no electricity supply and many more have no access to fixed networks. The companies responsible give no indication of when the problems will be fixed, creating great uncertainty. Even the government has admitted to huge hold-ups in the approval process for the thousands of applications for support, and many households have been forced to find solutions to their problems without any help. The government has also said that it has reallocated roughly EUR 500 million of RRP works that were planned in the areas affected. Given that this is a matter of fundamental rights, such as the right to health and decent housing, I would like to ask the following questions: 1.
Is the Commission monitoring the situation, including the rate at which issues are being resolved?
Has the Portuguese Government provided any information or requested support with regard to progressing with repair work?
Can the Commission confirm that the region will not be deprived of the investment planned under the RRP?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (1.7.2026) When it comes to EU instruments which can offer support, on 26 January 2026, Portugal activated the Copernicus Emergency Management Service - on demand mapping - to assess the situation during and after the event. Some maps were requested to detect the flooded area, and other products to provide damage assessment. The activation is still ongoing. Beyond the use of EU instruments, it is for the Member State to monitor the situation. On 13 April 2026, Portugal submitted an EU Solidarity Fund (EUSF)1 application regarding several consecutive storms in January and February 2026. In the application, Portugal provided information regarding the direct damages caused by the disaster. The Commission’s assessment of the application is ongoing. Following an amendment request by Portugal according to Article 21 of the Recovery and Resilience Facility regulation2, the Commission adopted on 18 May 2026 a proposal for a Council Implementing Decision amending the recovery and resilience plan (RRP) for Portugal3, which addressed inter alia the impact of natural disasters on the implementation of the RRP. According to this proposal, the overall allocation for the Portuguese RRP would not be modified. This revision of the Portuguese RRP was adopted by the Council on 12 June 2026.
1 Council Regulation (EC) No 2012/2002 of 11 November 2002 establishing the European Union Solidarity

Fund (OJ L 311, 14.11.2002, p. 3) as amended by Regulation (EU) No 661/2014 of the European Parliament and the Council of 15 May 2014 (OJ L 189, 27.6.2014, p. 143) and by Regulation (EU) 2020/461 of the European Parliament and the Council of 30 March 2020 (OJ L 99, 31.3.2020, p. 9); https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legalcontent/EN/TXT/?uri=celex:32002R2012. 2 Regulation (EU) 2021/241 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 12 February 2021 establishing the Recovery and Resilience Facility. 3 COM(2026) 248 final.
